A sorted array lets you binary-search in.zh: 有序数组支持 $O(\log n)$ 的二分查找，但插入为 $O(n)$，因为插入点之后的每个元素都必须后移。链表则将这一取舍反转：在已知位置插入为 $O(1)$，但查找为 $O(n)$。
A sorted array lets you binary-search in.src:
A sorted array lets you binary-search in $O(\log n)$ but
          insertion is $O(n)$ because every element after the
          insertion point has to shift. A linked list flips the
          trade: insertion is $O(1)$ at a known position, but search
          is $O(n)$.

A balanced binary tree gives you @@T0@@b.zh: 平衡二叉树能在 $O(\log n)$ 内同时提供@@T0@@两者@@T1@@。正是这一事实——有序插入与有序查找可在同一对数时间内完成——使得树无处不在地出现：从数据库索引（B 树）到 Dijkstra 与 A* 内部的优先队列（二叉堆），再到支撑现代文本编辑器的 rope 结构。
A balanced binary tree gives you @@T0@@b.src: A balanced binary tree gives you both in $O(\log n)$. That single fact — that you can support ordered insert and ordered search in the same logarithmic time — is the reason trees show up everywhere from database indexes (B-trees) to the priority queues inside Dijkstra and A* (binary heaps) to the rope structures that back modern text editors.

@@T0@@Two trees worth knowing well.@@T1@.zh: @@T0@@两种值得深入掌握的树。@@T1@@@@T2@@二叉搜索树@@T3@@（BST）维持左小右大的不变式——为有序查询而构建。@@T4@@堆@@T5@@维持父小于子的不变式——为「立刻给我最小/最大元素」而构建。二者形状相同，不变式却截然不同。树家族中的其余成员（AVL 树、红黑树、B 树、trie、线段树）都是这两个思想的细化。
@@T0@@Two trees worth knowing well.@@T1@.src: Two trees worth knowing well. The binary search tree (BST) maintains a left-less-than, right-greater invariant — built for ordered queries. The heap maintains a parent-less-than-children invariant — built for "give me the smallest/largest right now". Same shape, completely different invariant. The rest of the tree zoo (AVL, red-black, B-tree, trie, segment tree) are refinements of these two ideas.

A binary tree is a collection of @@T0@@n.src: A binary tree is a collection of nodes, each carrying a value and up to two children — left and right. One node is distinguished as the root; a node with no children is a leaf; the height is the longest path from root to leaf.

@@T0@@Pre-order@@T1@@ — root, then left,.zh: @@T0@@前序@@T1@@——根、左、右。用于@@T2@@序列化@@T3@@树（已知前序加中序即可唯一重建该树）。

@@T0@@In-order@@T1@@ — left, root, right.zh: @@T0@@中序@@T1@@——左、根、右。对 BST 而言，它按@@T2@@有序顺序@@T3@@给出各值——这是验证 BST 正确性最简洁的方式。

@@T0@@Post-order@@T1@@ — left, right, ro.src: Post-order — left, right, root. Used to free / evaluate bottom-up (every parent waits for its children).

The cost of every BST operation — insert.zh: 每次 BST 操作——插入、查找、前驱、中序后继、删除——的代价都与所触及节点的深度成正比。平衡树将深度上限控制在 $\log_2 n$；不平衡的树则可能让深度增长到 $n$。
The cost of every BST operation — insert.src:
The cost of every BST operation — insert, search,
          predecessor, in-order successor, delete — is proportional
          to the depth of the node touched. A balanced tree caps
          depth at $\log_2 n$; an unbalanced one can let it grow to
          $n$.

@@T0@@Red-black trees@@T1@@ use a colour.src: Red-black trees use a colour invariant that gives weaker balance but cheaper updates. This is what most standard libraries ship as their ordered map: C++ std::map, Java TreeMap, Linux kernel's process scheduler.

@@T0@@B-trees@@T1@@ generalise the idea.zh: @@T0@@B 树@@T1@@将这一思想推广到拥有众多子节点的节点，并针对磁盘块大小进行调优。你所用过的每一个关系数据库索引都是 B 树的变体。
@@T0@@B-trees@@T1@@ generalise the idea.src: B-trees generalise the idea to nodes with many children, tuned to disk-block sizes. Every relational database index you have ever used is a B-tree variant.

@@T0@@Treaps and skip lists@@T1@@ random.src: Treaps and skip lists randomise to get balance in expectation without rotations — simpler to implement, comparable performance.

@@T0@@The trap.@@T1@@\n A plain.zh: @@T0@@陷阱。@@T1@@未作平衡的朴素 BST 是一种@@T2@@糟糕透顶@@T3@@的通用数据结构——它的最坏情况由有序输入触发，而在实践中这比均匀随机输入更常见。在生产环境中应始终选用平衡变体。只有在为教学而实现它（如本文）或输入顺序可保证无对抗性时，才应选用朴素 BST。
@@T0@@The trap.@@T1@@\n A plain.src: The trap. A plain BST without balancing is a terrible general-purpose data structure — its worst case is hit by sorted input, which is more common than uniform random in practice. Always reach for a balanced variant in production. Reach for the plain BST only when implementing it for teaching (like this article) or when input order is guaranteed adversarial-free.

Heapify — building a heap in O(n).src: Heapify — building a heap in O(n)

The obvious way to build a heap of $n$ i.zh: 构建含 $n$ 个元素的堆，最直接的做法是调用 @@T0@@插入@@T1@@ $n$ 次。这需要 $n \log n$ 的工作量。Floyd 堆化则通过自底向上操作在 $O(n)$ 内完成。
The obvious way to build a heap of $n$ i.src: The obvious way to build a heap of $n$ items is to call insert $n$ times. That's $n \log n$ work. Floyd's heapify does it in $O(n)$ by working bottom-up.

Why $O(n)$ instead of $O(n \\log n)$? Si.zh: 为何是 $O(n)$ 而非 $O(n \log n)$？对深度为 $d$ 的节点做下滤，代价至多为 $h - d$，其中 $h = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$ 为树的高度。半数节点是叶（代价 0）；四分之一在上移一层处（代价 1）；八分之一在上移两层处（代价 2）；该级数求和收敛为一个常数乘以 $n$。点击上方的 @@T0@@堆化随机 12 个@@T1@@，观察自底向上的各趟处理。
Why $O(n)$ instead of $O(n \\log n)$? Si.src: Why $O(n)$ instead of $O(n \log n)$? Sift-down on a node at depth $d$ costs at most $h - d$ where $h = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$ is the tree's height. Half the nodes are leaves (cost 0); a quarter are one level up (cost 1); an eighth are two levels up (cost 2); the sum collapses to a constant times $n$. Press heapify random 12 above and watch the bottom-up passes.

Heapify is also the building block of @@.zh: 堆化也是@@T0@@堆排序@@T1@@的构建模块：原地构建最大堆（$O(n)$），再反复提取最大值并放入数组末尾槽位（$n \log n$）。总计 $O(n \log n)$，原地进行，无需辅助内存。它在多数语言中并非默认排序的原因在于缓存行为——尽管渐进复杂度相同，实践中快排与 Timsort 仍占主导。
Heapify is also the building block of @@.src: Heapify is also the building block of heap sort: build a max-heap in place ($O(n)$), then repeatedly extract-max into the last array slot ($n \log n$). Total $O(n \log n)$, in-place, no auxiliary memory. The reason it isn't the default sort in most languages is cache behaviour — quicksort and Timsort dominate in practice despite the same asymptotic.

@@T0@@Pointer-based vs array-based.@@T1@.zh: @@T0@@基于指针与基于数组。@@T1@@使用显式节点对象的 BST 需为指针追踪和较差的缓存局部性付出代价。对于小型固定规模树，将子节点存于平坦数组中（左孩子在 $2i+1$、右孩子在 $2i+2$——与堆相同的技巧）会快得多，尽管不平衡形状会带来空隙。
@@T0@@Pointer-based vs array-based.@@T1@.src: Pointer-based vs array-based. BSTs with explicit node objects pay for pointer chasing and poor cache locality. For small fixed-size trees, storing children in a flat array (left at $2i+1$, right at $2i+2$ — same trick as heaps) is much faster despite the gaps from unbalanced shapes.

@@T0@@Recursion depth limits.@@T1@@ A de.zh: @@T0@@递归深度限制。@@T1@@若采用朴素递归遍历，含 $n$ 个节点的退化树在多数语言中当 $n \approx 10^4$ 时就会使调用栈溢出。要么平衡树，要么改用显式栈的迭代形式。
@@T0@@Recursion depth limits.@@T1@@ A de.src: Recursion depth limits. A degenerate tree on $n$ nodes will overflow the call stack at $n \approx 10^4$ in most languages if you traverse with naïve recursion. Either balance the tree or use the iterative-with-explicit-stack form.

@@T0@@Two heaps for the running median.@.zh: @@T0@@用两个堆求滑动中位数。@@T1@@下半部分用最大堆、上半部分用最小堆，并保持两者大小平衡。插入与求中位数均花费 $O(\log n)$。这是一道经典的面试题，其解法是一种堆的配置，而非某种巧妙的新结构。
@@T0@@Two heaps for the running median.@.src: Two heaps for the running median. A max-heap of the lower half and a min-heap of the upper half, kept balanced in size. Insert and median both cost $O(\log n)$. A classic interview question whose solution is a heap configuration, not a clever new structure.

@@T0@@Knuth, @@T1@@The Art of Computer P.src: Knuth, The Art of Computer Programming, Vol 3. The reference, still. Trees are chapter 6.2.

meta.title: 树：逐枝展开
meta.tagline: BST、堆与遍历——构建它们、查询它们，观察上滤与下滤
meta.summary: 这种数据结构在幕后支撑着有序映射、优先队列、自动补全，以及算法教科书中的半壁江山。通过输入数值构建一棵二叉搜索树，观察四种不同顺序的遍历在其中穿行，再切换到堆，看上滤/下滤如何在每次插入与提取中维持堆不变式。
highlights: 通过输入数值构建 BST——当树平衡时，观察查找在 O(log n) 内命中匹配节点。
在同一棵树上动画演示全部四种遍历（前序、中序、后序、层序）。
实时最小堆与最大堆：插入触发上滤，提取最小值触发下滤，二者均逐步展示。
在 O(n) 内对随机数组堆化，观察自底向上算法如何胜过最直接的做法。
平衡为何重要：插入有序数值会得到链表（O(n) 查找）；随机顺序插入则得到 O(log n)。
